reject_reason: other: RSHash is a k-mer dictionary built on rank/select bitvectors and does not use an MPHF. Its only benchmark is against the SSHash k-mer dictionary (SSHash3 and SSHash5). There is no published comparison against std::unordered_map, CMPH, BBHash or any standalone MPHF, so it does not fit minimal-perfect-hash-functions.
tier_reason: This tier covers only the off-category comparison against SSHash. The Bioinformatics 2026 paper (btag440, Sec. 5.3-5.6, Tables 4-6) states an AMD EPYC 9454 CPU and GCC 12.2 in release mode. The flags (-O3 -march=native) are in source/CMakeLists.txt. The benchmark code is public (benchmarks/benchmark_rshash.sh plus the rshash bench/locate commands), and the SSHash side is pinned to commits 5a13d6a and e65dcb2.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Streaming lookups: RSHash is on average 1.4x and up to 2x faster than SSHash5. It queries 4.5x more k-mers/s on average, and up to 8.5x more, than the published SSHash3 (Table 4, Fig. 4). Single-k-mer lookups are on par with SSHash5: 0.5 us/k-mer (fast variant) and 0.6 us/k-mer (compact variant). Negative lookups are 50% faster and positive lookups are 10% slower (Table 5). Build is on average 60% faster with 40% less memory (Table 6; human 3:23 and 10.4 GB vs SSHash5 6:03 and 14.4 GB). All figures are verbatim from the paper.
corrections.caveats: The baseline is SSHash, another k-mer dictionary, not std::unordered_map, CMPH, BBHash or any MPHF. RSHash itself replaces the MPHF with rank/select bitvectors. Positive random single-k-mer lookups are 10% slower than SSHash5. test/hashtable.cpp can time std::unordered_set<uint64_t> streaming lookups, but no such numbers are published, and the benchmarks README describes that file as a correctness check. The repo was created 2025-02-17, not Feb 2026. It has 8 stars.

notes: All claimed numbers match the PMC page. The rejection is on category scope only. Under a k-mer-dictionary category with SSHash as baseline, this would be a valid Tier A entry. Repo metadata checked: MIT license, not a fork, not archived, 8 stars, last commit on main 2026-07-31 (active).

reject_reason: other: SSHash is a k-mer dictionary that uses PTHash internally, but every published benchmark compares it only against other k-mer dictionaries. The 2022 paper uses dBG-FM, Pufferfish and BLight. The 2026 paper (btag264) and jermp/kmer_sets_benchmark use SBWT and FMSI. No benchmark compares it against std::unordered_map, CMPH, BBHash or a standalone MPHF, so it does not fit minimal-perfect-hash-functions.
tier_reason: This tier covers only the off-category comparison. The peer-reviewed paper (Bioinformatics 38 Suppl. 1, Sec. 5, Tables 3-7) states gcc 11.2.0, -O3 -march=native and an Intel i9-9940X. Only the SSHash side of the harness is public (src/bench.cpp, src/query.cpp, script/benchmark_dictionary.sh at v1.0.0). The Pufferfish, BLight and dBG-FM runs have no published scripts or pinned commits, so the tier is B, not A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Human dataset, canonical SSHash, from Tables 4-7. Streaming membership: 253 ns/k-mer (high-hit) vs Pufferfish dense 402 and Blight b=0 440; 183 ns/k-mer (low-hit) vs 435 and 1,088. The paper summarizes this as 'comparable to or faster (by 2-3x) than Pufferfish and Blight'. Space: 9.39 bits/k-mer vs Pufferfish dense 45.04 and Blight b=0 20.17. Build: 16.2 min and 17.3 GB peak vs Pufferfish dense 70.7 min and 14.0 GB, and Blight 25.0 min and 7.5 GB. Random lookups: 990 ns positive and 854 ns negative, which is slower than Pufferfish dense (720 and 519) but faster than Blight b=0 (1,780 and 1,610).
corrections.hardware: Intel Core i9-9940X @ 3.30 GHz, 128 GB RAM, single core used; Ubuntu 19.10, Linux kernel 5.3.0, 64-bit
corrections.caveats: All comparisons are against other k-mer dictionaries (dBG-FM, Pufferfish, BLight; later SBWT and FMSI), never against std::unordered_map, CMPH, BBHash or a bare MPHF. Pufferfish dense is faster than SSHash on random lookups. SSHash wins on space (2-5x), on streaming queries (up to 2-3x) and on build time. No public harness or commit pins exist for the competitor runs in the 2022 paper. The newer benchmarks (jermp/kmer_sets_benchmark, benchmarks/README.md, Pibiri and Patro 2026) cover only SBWT and FMSI.

notes: The record's absolute numbers (990/854 ns, 9.39 bpk, 16.2 min, 17.3 GB) all appear in the paper, but they are not wins: SSHash is slower than Pufferfish dense on random lookup. The rejection is on category scope only. SSHash is notable (Bioconda, Rust port) and would qualify under a k-mer-dictionary category. Repo metadata checked: MIT license, not a fork, not archived, 109 stars, last commit 2026-09-03 (active).

reject_reason: other: BLight is a k-mer dictionary that uses BBHash internally. Its benchmarks compare it only against the Pufferfish k-mer index (Tables 1-2) and against the Squeakr and SRC abundance indexes, where BLight is slower to build. There is no comparison against std::unordered_map, CMPH, BBHash or a standalone MPHF, so it does not fit minimal-perfect-hash-functions.
tier_reason: This tier covers only the off-category comparison against Pufferfish. The peer-reviewed paper (Bioinformatics 37(18):2858, Tables 1-2) and the matching bioRxiv v4 preprint name the CPU (Xeon E5-2420) but state no compiler or flags. The repo's bench_blight.cpp times BLight alone, and its makefile uses unversioned g++, so the evidence cannot reach Tier A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Human genome, k=31. Table 1 (construction): BLight 10 min, 7.4 GB peak, 22.3 bits/k-mer vs Pufferfish dense 69 min, 27.4 GB, 55.59 bits/k-mer. BLight ran with 12 threads; its single-thread human build took 60 min. Table 2 (querying all reference k-mers): BLight 1,748 s single-thread vs Pufferfish '1.799' (presumably 1,799 s), and 155 s multi-threaded vs 655 s. The column is labelled 16T, but the text says 12 threads. On real reads (SRR5833294), single-thread BLight takes 1,577 s vs Pufferfish 1,260 s, so BLight is slower there. All figures are verbatim from the paper.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Not stated in the paper; repo makefile builds with g++ (version unstated) -DNDEBUG -Ofast -flto -march=native -mtune=native -msse4
corrections.caveats: BLight is compared only against Pufferfish, a k-mer index, not against std::unordered_map, BBHash or CMPH directly. The construction win compares BLight on 12 threads against Pufferfish. Single-thread queries are at parity on reference k-mers, and BLight is slower than Pufferfish on real reads (1,577 vs 1,260 s). BLight wins only multi-threaded, because Pufferfish queries do not scale with threads. In the abundance-index use case, BLight builds slower than SRC and Squeakr (19:49 vs 05:12 and 15:11) and wins only on memory. The paper states no compiler or flags. The repo was last pushed 2024-07-06 (stale).

notes: The claimed numbers match the published Tables 1-2. The OUP page came through WebFetch (curl gets 403) and matches bioRxiv 10.1101/546309v4. The rejection is on category scope only. Repo metadata checked: AGPL-3.0, not a fork, not archived, 36 stars, last commit 2024-07-06 (stale).
